description.narrative: 1. In March 2022, the Institute of Accountancy Arusha (IAA) to developed assessment tools for three (3) apprenticeship programmes at bachelor’s degree level. The assessment tools have enabled the piloting of three new quality apprenticeship programmes. The first group of apprenices will graduate by the end of 2023. 2. In March 2022, the State University of Zanzibar revised the assessment tool for apprenticeship programme at National Technical Award (NTA) Level 4 in hotel operations. The assessment tools have enabled the university to deliver quality apprenticeship programmes in tourism and hospitality to 70 new apprentices who will graduate in October 2023. With the support from the Norway funded Global programme on skills and lifelong learning – under Tanzania component TZA/22/50/NOR (108878), the ILO trained 40 supervisors in hotel operations on quality apprenticeships and equipped them with knowledge on supervision and assessment of apprentices while at their workplaces training. Further, in March 2022 the ILO facilitated workshops foe the revision of assessment tool (NTA Level 4) for apprenticeship programme in hotel operations. The assessment tools have enabled the university to deliver quality apprenticeship programmes in tourism and hospitality to 70 new apprentices who graduate in October 2023. In addition, the ILO provided financial support for the training of 40% of apprentices. Under the Tanzania component of the Norway funded Global programme on skills and lifelong learning – TZA/22/50/NOR (108878), the ILO in collaboration with the IAA reviewed the checklist for delivering quality apprenticeships and identified that the assessments needed to be done at both the workplace and in the classroom. The ILO facilitated workshops that enabled IAA to develop the two assessments. Most of the workplace assessments are done through an online system as a response and adjustment to COVID 19. Following the support, Institute of Accountancy Arusha (IAA) has developed and rolled out a full fledged 2 Bachelor Degrees with Apprenticeship ; 1) Bachelor of Banking with Apprenticeship 2) Bachelor of Insurance and Risk Management with Apprenticeship and 3) Bachelor of Tourism and Hospitality with Apprenticeship

description.narrative:
1. Sector Skills Strategy on Beef-Production sub-sector
From January 2022, the government by Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), in partnership Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC), the Tanzania Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture (TCCIA), Tanzania Meat Board (TMB) and other stakeholders developed a Sector Skills Strategy which addressing Business Capability Gaps in the Beef Production Sub-Sector in Tanzania. The strategy was informed by a pilot skills anticipation surveys conducted in selected priority sectors in Tanzania mainland. 2. National Action Plan for Improving and Strengthening Labour Market Information and Skills Anticipation in Tanzania From January 2022, the government led by Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC) from Zanzibar developed a national level action plan for improving and strengthening the LMI and skills anticipation system in Tanzania. This plan was informed by the government approved concept note for establishment National LMIS of September 2020 and report on “Skills Mismatch Survey in Selected Economic Sectors in Tanzania Mainland (Analytical Report, 2021). 1. Utilizing resources available under the SIFA-Skills Anticipation Project (RAF/19/01/DEU -107197), the ILO in November 2022 facilitated and provided technical support to the stakeholders meeting which validated Sector Skills Strategy on Beef-Production sub-sector. The Sector Skills Strategy developed by using the ILO skills anticipation methodology namely Rapid Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification (STED) methodology.
2. Under the technical support of the ILO and resources under SIFA project, From January 2022, the government led by President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC) in collaboration with other stakeholders conducted a mapping for improving Labour Market Information and Skills Anticipation systems, institutions, data infrastructure, capacities, and approaches in Zanzibar. The mapping identified and measured skills mismatches in determining the characteristics of the labour markets. Reviewed the establishment of the adequacy of the governance systems, the existing labour market and skills anticipation institutional and coordination arrangements.
3. The office further supported the Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC) and other key stakeholders developed and validated National Action Plan for Improving and Strengthening Labour Market Information and Skills Anticipation in Tanzania in November 2022

description.narrative:
1. Tripartite and inter-ministerial task force From January 2022 Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), in partnership Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC), and other sectoral ministries established a country level tripartite and inter-ministerial task force on skills anticipation with lead institutions in Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar
2. Capacities of national actors strengthened to improve LMI and skills anticipation system From April 2023 National level actors (Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), in partnership Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC)) and institutions (vocational training authorities, social security institutions, chambers of commerce), capacities strengthened to improve Labour Market Information and skills anticipation system. 1. With the support from SIFA-Skills Anticipation Project (RAF/19/01/DEU -107197), ILO social partners, Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), in consultation with the Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC), established a country level tripartite and inter-ministerial task force on skills anticipation with lead from ministries responsible for labour and employment for both Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar. Terms of references for the inter-ministerial institution were agreed upon to guide execution of their responsibilities
2. In the context of the same project; SIFA, the office implemented activities to build the capacities of the National level actors (Prime Minister’s Office – Labour Youth, Employment and Persons with Disabilities (PMO-LYED), in partnership Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) for mainland Tanzania and President’s Office - Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEI), Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC), and other stakeholders for both Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar to improve LMI and skills anticipation system, including workshops, hybridge virtual and physical engagements and trainings, as well as online trainings from April 2023

description.narrative: In September 2022, the Vocational Education and Training Authority (VETA) developed five (5) Recognition of Prior Learning (PRL) assessment tools. The tools were developed to facilitate the extension of RPL programmes into five occupations namely plant operator, housekeeping, laboratory assistant, heavy duty equipment maintenance and meat processing technology. The tools will be piloted and finalized by October 2023. With the support from the Norway funded Global Programme on Skills and Lifelong Learning – Tanzania component with project code: TZA/20/51/NOR (107956) for 2021-22 and TZA/22/50/NOR (108878) for 2023-24. The ILO facilitated the capacity building of RPL assessors in five occupations and supported the designing and drafting of the five new RPL assessment tools. ILO will also support the piloting be piloted and finalization of the tools by October 2023.
